agent-pipeline <version> init · <repo root>

Wrote:
  .gitignore: added `.worktrees/` and `.agent-pipeline/`
  agent-pipeline.json: created, with every setting left at its default
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: written
  CLAUDE.md: created, pointing at docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md

GitHub:
  labels: created needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent
  merges: squash merging is on, and no other merge setting was touched

Checked:
  ✓ `gh` is authenticated
  ✓ `claude` runs
  ✗ the `mattpocock-skills` plugin is not installed — an implement Stage has no skill without it
  ✓ a CI workflow is present in `.github/workflows`
  ✓ a Check is configured or inferable: npm test, npm run typecheck

Not ready: 1 item is yours to put right.

The first line names the Version doing the setting up (ADR-0007), in the shape
`run-summary.txt` describes, so a Target can be told which pipeline wrote the
files it is about to gain. Where a newer Version has been published, one line
follows it and nothing comes between them:

agent-pipeline <version> init · <repo root>
A newer Version is out: 0.5.0, and this is 0.4.0 — upgrade with `npm install -g "github:jjongs2/agent-pipeline#semver:*"`.

Wrote:
  ...

It is the same line a Run prints, under the same conditions, and like a Run's it
refuses nothing: `init` sets the Target up either way.

Three groups, always in this order and always all three, however little each has
to say.

`Wrote:` has one line per file that changed, and `  nothing to write` when the
Target already had everything — which is what a second `init` prints. The
conventions document is the one file rewritten rather than left alone, and it
carries the Version that wrote it in a hidden marker on its first line, which is
read before its text is compared (ADR-0007). Four lines, one per case:

  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: written
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: overwritten, because the copy here carried no Version
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: overwritten, because the copy here was left by 0.3.0
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: left alone, because 0.5.0 set this Target up and this is 0.4.0 — upgrade `agent-pipeline` to rewrite it

A copy marked with the same Version is compared as text and rewritten where it
differs, as `overwritten, because the copy here said something else`; identical
text is not a line at all. A copy a newer pipeline wrote is the one this never
touches: rewriting it would take the Target backwards, so it is left and the
upgrade is named. None of the four is a `Checked:` item, so none of them changes
the exit code — a Target is not unready for carrying another Version's copy.

`GitHub:` says which labels were created, or that every one of them was already
there, and that squash merging is on. Where GitHub could not be asked at all,
its one line is: nothing done: `gh` is not authenticated.

`Checked:` is one line per item only the human can put right, each marked `✓` or
`✗`, in a fixed order: `gh`, `claude`, the plugin, a CI workflow, a Check.

The last line is the exit code in words: `Ready: everything a Run expects of
this Target is in place.` for 0, and `Not ready: <n> items are yours to put
right.` for 1.
